#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <climits>

using namespace std;

int main() {
    string s;
    cin >> s;
    
    // Find all positions of "at" and "dot" in the string
    vector<int> atPositions;
    vector<int> dotPositions;
    
    // Find all "at" occurrences
    for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < s.length(); i++) {
        if (s[i] == 'a' && s[i+1] == 't') {
            atPositions.push_back(i);
        }
    }
    
    // Find all "dot" occurrences
    for (size_t i = 0; i + 2 < s.length(); i++) {
        if (s[i] == 'd' && s[i+1] == 'o' && s[i+2] == 't') {
            dotPositions.push_back(i);
        }
    }
    
    // We need exactly one '@' and the rest should be dots
    // Try each "at" as the single '@' position
    string bestResult = "";
    int minLength = INT_MAX;
    
    for (int atIdx : atPositions) {
        // Check if this "at" can be the '@' (not at beginning or end)
        if (atIdx == 0 || atIdx + 1 == (int)s.length() - 1) {
            continue;
        }
        
        // Build the result with this "at" replaced by '@'
        string candidate = s;
        
        // Replace "at" at position atIdx with '@'
        candidate.replace(atIdx, 2, "@");
        
        // Now replace all "dot" that don't overlap with '@' position
        // We need to be careful about overlapping positions
        vector<bool> replaced(candidate.length(), false);
        
        // Mark the '@' position as replaced
        replaced[atIdx] = true;
        replaced[atIdx + 1] = true;
        
        // Process "dot" occurrences from left to right
        for (int dotPos : dotPositions) {
            // Skip if this "dot" overlaps with already replaced positions
            if (dotPos >= atIdx && dotPos < atIdx + 2) continue; // overlaps with '@'
            if (dotPos + 2 >= atIdx && dotPos + 2 < atIdx + 2) continue;
            
            // Check if positions are already replaced
            if (replaced[dotPos] || replaced[dotPos+1] || replaced[dotPos+2]) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if this "dot" is at the beginning or end of the string
            if (dotPos == 0 || dotPos + 2 == (int)s.length() - 1) {
                continue; // Skip "dot" at beginning or end
            }
            
            // Replace this "dot"
            candidate.replace(dotPos, 3, ".");
            replaced[dotPos] = true;
            replaced[dotPos+1] = true;
            replaced[dotPos+2] = true;
        }
        
        // Check if the result is valid
        if (candidate[0] == '.' || candidate[0] == '@' || 
            candidate[candidate.length()-1] == '.' || candidate[candidate.length()-1] == '@') {
            continue;
        }
        
        // Check that there's exactly one '@'
        int atCount = 0;
        for (char c : candidate) {
            if (c == '@') atCount++;
        }
        if (atCount != 1) continue;
        
        // Check that we have a valid email (contains at least one dot in the domain part)
        size_t atPosInCandidate = candidate.find('@');
        if (atPosInCandidate == string::npos) continue;
        
        string domain = candidate.substr(atPosInCandidate + 1);
        if (domain.find('.') == string::npos && domain.length() > 0) {
            // This is acceptable - domain can be just letters without dots
            // But let's check if we missed any valid "dot" replacements
        }
        
        // Check length and lexicographic order
        if (candidate.length() < minLength || 
            (candidate.length() == minLength && candidate < bestResult)) {
            minLength = candidate.length();
            bestResult = candidate;
        }
    }
    
    // If no valid result found with the above approach, try to handle edge cases
    if (bestResult.empty()) {
        // Try to find any valid transformation
        // This handles cases where there might be no valid "at" position
        // But according to problem, input should be transformable
        
        // As fallback, try replacing first valid "at" and all valid "dot"s
        for (int atIdx : atPositions) {
            if (atIdx == 0 || atIdx + 1 == (int)s.length() - 1) continue;
            
            string candidate = s;
            candidate.replace(atIdx, 2, "@");
            
            // Replace all remaining "dot" that don't overlap with '@'
            for (int i = (int)candidate.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
                if (i + 2 < (int)candidate.length() && 
                    candidate[i] == 'd' && candidate[i+1] == 'o' && candidate[i+2] == 't') {
                    // Check if this "dot" is at beginning or end of original string
                    if (i == 0 || i + 2 == (int)s.length() - 1) continue;
                    // Check if overlaps with '@'
                    if (i >= atIdx && i < atIdx + 2) continue;
                    
                    candidate.replace(i, 3, ".");
                }
            }
            
            // Validate
            if (candidate[0] != '.' && candidate[0] != '@' && 
                candidate[candidate.length()-1] != '.' && candidate[candidate.length()-1] != '@') {
                int atCount = 0;
                for (char c : candidate) if (c == '@') atCount++;
                if (atCount == 1) {
                    if (bestResult.empty() || candidate.length() < bestResult.length() ||
                        (candidate.length() == bestResult.length() && candidate < bestResult)) {
                        bestResult = candidate;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    cout << bestResult;
    return 0;
}
